- **self**: Focused ultrasound thalamotomy and pallidotomy (18/5)

## How it works

- [statement] The 2024 pallidotomy meta-analysis pooled post-treatment changes against baseline in a single-arm analysis because it could not compare against a sham/control group. Its pooled improvements therefore should not be interpreted as sham-adjusted treatment effects. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11422448/ · keywords: Focused ultrasound thalamotomy and pallidotomy
- [statement] Thalamotomy can cause persistent neurological deficits. The randomized trial reported persistent paresthesia and ataxia, and the prescriber information describes serious hemiparesis linked to edema and lesion extension toward the internal capsule. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5822192/ · keywords: Focused ultrasound thalamotomy and pallidotomy · also: https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/cdrh_docs/pdf15/P150038S006D.pdf

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Focused ultrasound thalamotomy is an ablative treatment directed at medication-refractory tremor in tremor-dominant Parkinson disease; pallidotomy targets GPi for motor complications, including dyskinesia. (high confidence) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/cdrh_docs/pdf15/P150038S037B.pdf · keywords: Focused ultrasound thalamotomy and pallidotomy · also: https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/scripts/cdrh/cfdocs/cfpma/pma.cfm?id=P150038S014
- [statement] FDA supplement S014, decided October 29, 2021, approved unilateral Exablate Neuro pallidotomy as an adjunct to medication for advanced idiopathic Parkinson disease with medication-refractory moderate to severe motor complications, age at least 30. (medium confidence) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/scripts/cdrh/cfdocs/cfpma/pma.cfm?id=P150038S014 · keywords: Focused ultrasound thalamotomy and pallidotomy · also: https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/cdrh_docs/pdf15/P150038S037B.pdf
- [statement] The 2022 EAN/MDS-ES guideline on invasive therapies states that unilateral MRgFUS of the STN can be considered for distinctly unilateral Parkinson's disease within registries, and its clinical-consensus statements say that unilateral MRgFUS of the thalamus for medication-resistant tremor of Parkinson's disease can be considered only within registries. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35791766/ · keywords: Focused ultrasound thalamotomy and pallidotomy

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] In the 27-patient pilot randomized thalamotomy trial, the on-medication treated-hand tremor subscore improved a median 62% after ultrasound versus 22% after sham at 3 months; this is a score reduction, not a percentage of patients cured. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5822192/ · keywords: Focused ultrasound thalamotomy and pallidotomy
- [statement] The pallidotomy randomized trial enrolled 94 patients; 65 active-treatment and 22 control patients completed primary assessment. At 3 months, 45 (69%) versus 7 (32%) responded. Response meant at least a 3-point reduction in treated-side off-medication MDS-UPDRS III or on-medication UDysRS, rather than requiring both. (low confidence) — https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2202721 · keywords: Focused ultrasound thalamotomy and pallidotomy · also: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36812432/
- [statement] The FDA thalamotomy labeling specifies unilateral ventral intermediate thalamic treatment for medication-refractory tremor in tremor-dominant Parkinson’s disease, in patients at least age 30; it is a tremor indication rather than an indication for all Parkinsonian symptoms. (medium confidence) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/cdrh_docs/pdf15/P150038S006D.pdf · keywords: Focused ultrasound thalamotomy and pallidotomy · also: https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/cdrh_docs/pdf15/P150038S037B.pdf
- [statement] Sources differ on unilateral focused ultrasound pallidotomy for Parkinson's disease: the 2022 EAN/MDS-ES guideline's clinical-consensus statement says that unilateral MRgFUS of the pallidum is not recommended, whereas the FDA PMA record for Exablate Neuro lists approval of unilateral pallidotomy for advanced idiopathic Parkinson's disease with a decision date of 10/29/2021, and the NEJM sham-controlled trial reports a response in 45 patients (69%) after ablation versus 7 (32%) after sham. The sources carry different dates, evidence bases and jurisdictions and are recorded side by side, not reconciled. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35791766/ · keywords: Focused ultrasound thalamotomy and pallidotomy · also: https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/scripts/cdrh/cfdocs/cfpma/pma.cfm?id=P150038S014, https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2202721

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Thalamotomy trial safety findings included two cases of mild hemiparesis from internal-capsule heating that improved, alongside persistent orofacial paresthesia, finger paresthesia and ataxia. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5822192/ · keywords: Focused ultrasound thalamotomy and pallidotomy
- [statement] Pallidotomy durability was assessed in an open-label extension: 30 of 39 assessed initial responders still responded at 12 months. This denominator excludes initial nonresponders and unassessed responders. (low confidence) — https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2202721 · keywords: Focused ultrasound thalamotomy and pallidotomy
- [statement] Pallidotomy-related adverse events included dysarthria, gait disturbance, loss of taste, visual disturbance and facial weakness; investigators called for longer and larger trials. (medium confidence) — https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2202721 · keywords: Focused ultrasound thalamotomy and pallidotomy · also: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36812432/, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11422448/
- [statement] The July 3, 2025 FDA S037 expansion concerns pallidothalamic tractotomy, including a contralateral procedure staged at least 6 months later in eligible patients aged at least 30. It must not be described as blanket approval of bilateral GPi pallidotomy or bilateral Parkinson thalamotomy. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2025-07-03) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/cdrh_docs/pdf15/P150038S037B.pdf · keywords: Focused ultrasound thalamotomy and pallidotomy · also: https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/scripts/cdrh/cfdocs/cfpma/pma.cfm?id=P150038S014
- [statement] NICE HTG733, published December 18, 2024, restricts focused ultrasound thalamotomy for moderate-to-severe Parkinson’s tremor to formal research approved by a research ethics committee. That NHS recommendation is jurisdiction-specific and should be distinguished from FDA device approval. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2024-12-18) — https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/htg733/chapter/1-Recommendations · keywords: Focused ultrasound thalamotomy and pallidotomy · also: https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/cdrh_docs/pdf15/P150038S037B.pdf
- [statement] MR-guided focused ultrasound thalamotomy and pallidotomy are lesioning procedures: focused acoustic energy heats and ablates a selected brain target, with MRI thermometry and clinical testing guiding delivery. Incisionless delivery still entails destruction of brain tissue. (medium confidence) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/cdrh_docs/pdf15/P150038S006D.pdf · keywords: Focused ultrasound thalamotomy and pallidotomy · also: https://www.e-jmd.org/journal/view.php?number=583
- [statement] Durability and generalizability remain uncertain: the pallidotomy trial called for longer and larger studies, and the systematic review recommends follow-up beyond one year with larger samples and controlled, blinded designs. (medium confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36812432/ · keywords: Focused ultrasound thalamotomy and pallidotomy · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11422448/
- [statement] Patient selection requires more than symptom severity: the tremor-dominant Parkinson’s prescriber information requires MRI suitability, ability to tolerate and communicate during treatment, and screening for bleeding risks, prolonged immobilization and skull-density constraints. (medium confidence) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/cdrh_docs/pdf15/P150038S006D.pdf · keywords: Focused ultrasound thalamotomy and pallidotomy · also: https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/cdrh_docs/pdf15/P150038S037B.pdf
- [statement] Exact skull-density eligibility must be taken from the relevant labeling: the June 2018 tremor-dominant Parkinson’s prescriber document lists 0.45 (±0.05) or less, whereas the July 2025 S037 document lists less than 0.40. These target- and revision-specific documents should not be collapsed into one universal cutoff. (medium confidence) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/cdrh_docs/pdf15/P150038S006D.pdf · keywords: Focused ultrasound thalamotomy and pallidotomy · also: https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/cdrh_docs/pdf15/P150038S037B.pdf

## Research summary — Focused ultrasound thalamotomy and pallidotomy

Focused ultrasound creates targeted thermal lesions for selected Parkinson symptoms. Thalamotomy evidence concerns medication-refractory tremor; pallidotomy evidence concerns motor complications and dyskinesia. Sham-controlled trials show symptom benefits but also neurological adverse events, and longer-term controlled evidence remains limited. US target-specific approvals and NICE research-only recommendations need separate interpretation. The 2025 US bilateral expansion addresses staged pallidothalamic tractotomy, a distinct target.
